(frog-mo)=
# frog-mo

<!-- Generated by generate_readme.py from the CLI definitions in src/frogchem/cli. Do not edit by hand. -->

{bdg-primary}`Parsing` Analyse the atomic-orbital composition of molecular orbitals (ORCA and Gaussian outputs).

## What it does

Molecular orbitals (MOs) are combinations of atomic orbitals. This command tells you, in %, which
atoms and which kind of atomic orbital (s, p, d, f) make up each MO: is the HOMO a lone pair on N
or a π orbital of the ring? Is the LUMO of a complex metal d or ligand π*? How much metal d is
in the frontier orbitals? Use it to describe frontier orbitals in a paper, to understand an
excitation found by `frog-tddft` (which lists transitions like H→L), or to check orbital
character before plotting an orbital cube with `frog-density`.

## Input

An output that **contains all the MO coefficients** (they are not printed by default; a single
point on the final geometry is enough):

* **ORCA**: add `! PrintBasis PrintMOs` to the input.
* **Gaussian 16**: `#p ... pop=full iop(3/33=1) iop(6/80=1) gfinput` (the same route serves
  `frog-density`, `frog-charges`, `frog-tddft --dct` and `frog-nbo --cube`). `pop=full`
  prints every MO (the default population prints only a few); pure (`5D 7F`) and Cartesian
  (`6D 10F`) d/f functions are both read, g functions are not.

Open-shell (UKS/UHF) outputs have separate α and β orbitals (`--beta`). MO numbers are
**0-based** (ORCA's numbering; Gaussian's MO 1 is MO 0 here), atom numbers too.

### Arguments

**Positional arguments**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `file` … | required | ORCA output files (with ! PrintBasis PrintMOs) or Gaussian logs (with pop=full) |

**Options**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-i`, `--indices` `INDICES …` |  | Atom indices to show (0-based) |
| `--elements` `EL …` |  | Show all atoms of these elements, e.g. 'C' 'Fe' |
| `--orbital-type` `TYPE …` |  | Restrict to these orbital types: s, p, d, f (the heatmap also accepts px, dxy, ...) |
| `-b`, `--buffer` `BUFFER` |  | Number of MOs shown on each side of the HOMO (all MOs if omitted) |
| `--beta` |  | Use beta orbitals (open-shell calculations) |

**Plot options**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--plot` `[PATH]` |  | Save the plot; PATH is optional (default: <stem>_mo.png) |
| `--fig-format` `{png,svg,pdf,eps}` | `png` | Image format, unless the path already has an extension |
| `--dpi` `DPI` | `300` | Raster resolution of saved plots |
| `--show` |  | Also open the plot in an interactive window |
| `--title` `TEXT` |  | Plot title ('' removes it) |
| `--xlabel` `TEXT` |  | Label of the x axis |
| `--ylabel` `TEXT` |  | Label of the y axis |
| `--xlim` `MIN MAX` |  | Range of the x axis |
| `--ylim` `MIN MAX` |  | Range of the y axis |
| `--colors` `COLOR …` |  | Colours of the plotted series, in order (matplotlib names or #hex) |
| `--linewidth` `W` |  | Line width in points |
| `--linestyle` `{solid,dashed,dotted,dashdot}` |  | Line style |
| `--legend`, `--no-legend` |  | Show or hide the legend (default: decided by the plot) |
| `--grid`, `--no-grid` |  | Show or hide the grid (default: decided by the plot) |
| `--figsize` `W H` |  | Figure size in inches |
| `--font-size` `PT` |  | Base font size in points (titles and labels scale with it) |
| `--cmap` `NAME` | `rocket_r` | Colormap of maps and heatmaps (matplotlib or seaborn name) |

**Output**

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--out-dir` `DIR` |  | Directory for per-input output files (default: next to each input file) |

Shared by every command: `-v/--verbose`, `-q/--quiet`, `--format {table,json,csv}`, `--table-file PATH` — see [CLI conventions](conventions.md).

## Output

| Kind | Name | When | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Terminal | `MO Composition (%) (<file>)` | always | One row per MO: energy (eV), occupation and % contribution per atom/shell and per shell type |
| Plot | `<stem>_mo.png` | `--plot` | Heatmap of the % contribution of each basis function to each MO (<stem>_mo_beta.png with --beta) |

### How to read it

A table with one row per MO: **MO** index, **E (eV)**, **Occ** (2 = doubly occupied, 1 = singly
occupied in an open-shell α/β set, 0 = virtual), then the % of each selected atom and shell
(`6N_p` = p functions of atom 6, a nitrogen) and the totals per shell type (`Total_s`, `Total_p`...).

* Percentages are the squared MO coefficients normalised to 100 % per MO (C² analysis, overlap
  between basis functions ignored). They are a good qualitative picture; they differ from the
  Mulliken or Löwdin orbital populations printed by some programs, especially with diffuse basis sets.
* The atom columns appear only for systems with up to 10 atoms, or for the atoms selected with
  `-i`/`--elements`; with many MOs and no `-b`, only HOMO−5 … HOMO+5 are tabulated.
* Contributions spread over many atoms are normal for delocalised (π, Rydberg-like) orbitals.
* With `--beta`, the MO window and the HOMO box of the plot are currently centred on the **α**
  HOMO (for a doublet, the β HOMO is one MO lower): check the **Occ** column to find the β HOMO.

Example (water, B3LYP/def2-TZVPP, `-b 2`): MO 4 = HOMO, −8.54 eV, 99.37 % O p (the out-of-plane
lone pair); MO 5 = LUMO, +0.52 eV, 47.91 % O s and 23.3 % on each H s (σ* O–H).

## Step by step

1. Start with `frog-mo mol.out -b 3`: composition of the MOs from HOMO−3 to HOMO+3 (the LUMO is HOMO+1).
2. For a large molecule pick the atoms you care about with `-i 0 1` (0-based) or `--elements Fe N`, and the shell with `--orbital-type d`; otherwise only per-shell totals are shown.
3. Add `--plot` (optionally `--plot mo.svg`) to save a heatmap of every basis function vs MO; the HOMO column is boxed in cyan.
4. Open shell: run once as is (α orbitals) and once with `--beta`.

## Full reference

Every option, as printed by `frog-mo --help`:

:::{dropdown} `frog-mo --help`
```text
usage: frog-mo [-h] [-v] [-q] [--format {table,json,csv}] [--table-file PATH]
               [-i INDICES [INDICES ...]] [--elements EL [EL ...]]
               [--orbital-type TYPE [TYPE ...]] [-b BUFFER] [--beta] [--out-dir DIR]
               [--plot [PATH]] [--fig-format {png,svg,pdf,eps}] [--dpi DPI] [--show]
               [--title TEXT] [--xlabel TEXT] [--ylabel TEXT] [--xlim MIN MAX] [--ylim MIN MAX]
               [--colors COLOR [COLOR ...]] [--linewidth W]
               [--linestyle {solid,dashed,dotted,dashdot}] [--legend | --no-legend]
               [--grid | --no-grid] [--figsize W H] [--font-size PT] [--cmap NAME]
               file [file ...]

Analyse the atomic-orbital composition of molecular orbitals (ORCA and Gaussian outputs).

Prints the % contribution of each atom and shell (s, p, d, f) to the MOs around the HOMO, and
optionally saves a heatmap of the full MO coefficient matrix.

positional arguments:
  file                          ORCA output files (with ! PrintBasis PrintMOs) or Gaussian logs
                                (with pop=full)

options:
  -h, --help                    show this help message and exit
  -i INDICES [INDICES ...], --indices INDICES [INDICES ...]
                                Atom indices to show (0-based)
  --elements EL [EL ...]        Show all atoms of these elements, e.g. 'C' 'Fe'
  --orbital-type TYPE [TYPE ...]
                                Restrict to these orbital types: s, p, d, f (the heatmap also
                                accepts px, dxy, ...)
  -b BUFFER, --buffer BUFFER    Number of MOs shown on each side of the HOMO (all MOs if omitted)
  --beta                        Use beta orbitals (open-shell calculations)

plot options:
  --plot [PATH]                 Save the plot; PATH is optional (default: <stem>_mo.png)
  --fig-format {png,svg,pdf,eps}
                                Image format, unless the path already has an extension (default:
                                png)
  --dpi DPI                     Raster resolution of saved plots (default: 300)
  --show                        Also open the plot in an interactive window
  --title TEXT                  Plot title ('' removes it)
  --xlabel TEXT                 Label of the x axis
  --ylabel TEXT                 Label of the y axis
  --xlim MIN MAX                Range of the x axis
  --ylim MIN MAX                Range of the y axis
  --colors COLOR [COLOR ...]    Colours of the plotted series, in order (matplotlib names or #hex)
  --linewidth W                 Line width in points
  --linestyle {solid,dashed,dotted,dashdot}
                                Line style
  --legend, --no-legend         Show or hide the legend (default: decided by the plot)
  --grid, --no-grid             Show or hide the grid (default: decided by the plot)
  --figsize W H                 Figure size in inches
  --font-size PT                Base font size in points (titles and labels scale with it)
  --cmap NAME                   Colormap of maps and heatmaps (matplotlib or seaborn name)
                                (default: rocket_r)

output:
  -v, --verbose                 Enable debug output
  -q, --quiet                   Suppress banner, info and saved-file messages
  --format {table,json,csv}     Format of the tables printed on stdout (default: table)
  --table-file PATH             Also write all tables to PATH (.json, .csv or .txt; otherwise the
                                --format is used)
  --out-dir DIR                 Directory for per-input output files (default: next to each input
                                file)

outputs:
  terminal (stdout; --format table|json|csv, --table-file PATH):
    MO Composition (%) (<file>)
                                One row per MO: energy (eV), occupation and % contribution per
                                atom/shell and per shell type
  plots (saved, not shown; --fig-format, --dpi, --show):
    <stem>_mo.png               [--plot] Heatmap of the % contribution of each basis function to
                                each MO (<stem>_mo_beta.png with --beta)

examples:
  frog-mo opt.out -b 5
      Composition of HOMO-5 ... LUMO+5
  frog-mo opt.out -i 0 1 --orbital-type d --plot
      d contributions of atoms 0 and 1, plus heatmap
  frog-mo opt.out --elements Fe -b 3 --plot fe_mo.svg
      Fe contributions around the HOMO, heatmap as SVG

Data go to stdout, messages to stderr. Atom indices are 0-based unless stated otherwise.
Step-by-step guide (what it is for, what you need, what to expect): docs/cli/frog-mo.md.
```
